newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen up early next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen up early next week.

text.p: The Polish bourse should rise early next week, recovering from this week's 3.1-percent profit-taking correction, but analysts were not sure if later demand would prove strong enough to continue the recent surge.

"Monday and Tuesday will test demand. Yesterday and today tested supply, which is falling, and now the question is if there'll be demand on Monday and Tuesday...If not, growth could end after one or two sessions," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.

Analysts said primary market offers next month, such as the initial public offerings of paintmaker Polifarb Debica SA and electrode maker Zaklady Elektrod Weglowych SA (ZEW), could prevent the recent stock-buying frenzy from returning.
The offers will be worth at least 38.5 million zlotys and 28 million zlotys respectively.

Before this week's dip to 16,105.5 points at Friday's close the main WIG index had risen 27 percent since mid-December on apparent foreign buying from institutional investors acting on their fresh picks for 1997.

"There could be falls in the second half of the week....There certainly shouldn't be growth because there are ever more offers on the primary market...which are starting to become larger and more attactive," said Remigiusz Tarka, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
But Tarka said the market might simply stabilise, as the institutions who bought shares over the past two months had no reason to suddenly pull out.
Analysts said the recent heightened activity of foreign investors on the bourse made the Polish market ever more dependent on moves on major Western exchanges.

They said the bourse could also be hurt if banks, which make up about 40 percent of market capitalisation, continue to suffer after the central bank's decision on Monday to raise obligatory reserves on zloty call and currency deposits.
Among the bourse's heaviest weighted banks, BPH fell the most this week, losing 9.8 percent.

Analysts said the market would likely not place too much emphasis on food prices for January's second ten days due early next week, as the central bank had said an interest rate rise was now not forthcoming.
Recent top gaining computer maker Optimus was finally hit by profit taking this week, falling 8.5 percent.
